findings.body:
Gain 5, Work 2, Harm 3
Raise: Not done
Case: normal use - a quiet pytest assertion fails and a later test hangs until the CI job is cancelled.
The previous finding remains open. Pytest writes the `F` progress mark without a newline ([pytest terminal reporter](https://github.com/pytest-dev/pytest/blob/9.0.2/src/_pytest/terminal.py#L615-L625)), while `fasttest.test_output` buffers incomplete lines until a newline or process exit (`src/forge/fasttest.py:683-695`). If cancellation terminates Forge while the test is still running, the mark never reaches the GitHub log. `_product_failure` then sees no failure, and `_restart` retries the cancelled job; a transient assertion can pass on that retry and leave CI green. The proof supplies a newline-terminated `F` directly in the fake GitHub log (`tests/test_ci_retries_failed_test_jobs.py:66`), so it misses the buffering path.

why: Forge reruns failed CI test jobs once (close's 'Started the failed test jobs again once') and reruns failed test files inside a group, even when a test failed its assertion. In Forge's last 150 runs, 0 of 38 job reruns passed and reruns cost 28% of CI time. Owner chose on 21 Nov 2026: rerun only on infrastructure errors.
